text: What makes a great adventurer dance for joy in the streets, his eyes gleaming with excitement and hollering like a child?
A movie.
If they knew that "Fortunes of Adventure" was the movie that guided this man onto the path of adventure, I think most people would not be surprised.

Now, this decades-old movie is getting a re-release in the cinema. Die-hard fan Joseph had bought a whole book of tickets, and was using every opportunity—including when playing Mahjong—to rave about it. I happened to be free the day of the first screening, so went along with him.
The re-release naturally makes old fans happy, but what really makes Joseph ecstatic was the news announced by the producer at the end of the screening...
It took over half an hour for Joseph's excitement to dissipate, or at least calm down to a manageable level. While he rests against a wall, I go to pick up some drinks from a nearby vending machine.
Hmm... I don't have much planned for tomorrow, so might as well make the most of this chance. After all, an all-night screening should be fun.
I feel so dumb after learning that the so-called "foreshadowing" was just a blooper, for I was really pondering when watching "Fortunes of Adventure 2"...
Joseph gets up and grabs an old-looking videotape from the shelf.
He fast-forwards, before pausing on a scene where the protagonist is surrounded by a group of sailors. Smiling, he points at someone in the corner.
{character:player} I... Where have I seen this face before?
I look carefully at the man on the screen, then turn to face Joseph.
As he intentionally pulls the same face as the man, I'm sure I'm on the right track.
Joseph goes into the kitchen and opens the fridge, but closes it again after taking one look. He turns around, scratching his neck a little awkwardly.
Did I say something weird? Even George, who has been eating quietly beside me, tilts his head to look at me.
Joseph pulls up a photo on his phone. It shows a room, piled high with all manner of strange trinkets.
...I think this is the first time I've ever seen Joseph so serious.
George spreads his wings and pats me on the shoulder, then closes his eyes and shakes his head. His little noises seem to say "Chill out, man. It's not this guy's first rodeo."
It's not a question of luck... There's a lot of valuable stuff in there.
Watching Joseph gently swipe the screen of his phone, it is like I can peer through time. I can perfectly imagine him carefully wiping those "trophies" in the past.
...I rack my brain, but can't for the life of me understand what Joseph means by his strange remark.
It's hard for people to visualize things they've never seen before, and I certainly can't imagine what this overwhelmingly positive and optimistic guy was like when depressed.

That afternoon, the two discussed adventures and travel while they ate. Although Joseph hadn't gone out for a while, and had only old stories to tell, it was still an eye-opening experience for his friend.

As they talked, Joseph pulled out a curiously-patterned ornament. His friend played around with it for a while, and seemed unable to put it down. Seeing that he couldn't tear himself away from it, Joseph simply gave it to him to keep.

His largess caused his friend to tease him, that he didn't care enough about his treasures to give them away so casually. But Joseph told him to treat it as an early birthday present, laughingly saying "Not so casual now, is it?"
Watching his friend leave, humming happily, he thought the little ornament looked even better hanging from his friend's waist.

The last bit of Joseph's reluctance disappeared along with his friend. "There's nothing to regret. Who's to say there won't be something better, just around the corner?" Thinking this, his entire being somehow felt lighter.
He suddenly recalled the words of a somewhat dissolute gentleman in a book he had once read.
"People only think of possessing, little realizing they are possessed."
While Joseph didn't appreciate this gentleman's cynical attitude, this was one saying which did somewhat resonate with him now.
"Memories hinder the future, and allow the past to invade."
And so it was that, after a sleepless night, Joseph began to go out with his treasures.
Some he gave to friends, while some he left in the street market for others to discover.
Gradually, more and more space was cleared in his home, until it was practically empty.
He was no longer trapped by nostalgia, by all the "memories" attached to things, and his old haunts took on a different look in his eyes.
As for the new treasures? He gave most of them away to people he meet as a token of their friendship after sharing the adventure stories related to the treasures...
After hearing such profoundly heartfelt words, I feel like now I really know this man in front of me...
I still have many thoughts fluttering around my mind, but right now I can't think of a better word for him than "awesome".
Joseph... My super adventurer.

Actually, I think Joseph really is embarrassed. After manically praising him so emotionally, even I'm now embarrassed for gushing so much myself, to say nothing of how he must feel! It's just his personality makes it almost easy for him to admit this.

Luckily, Joseph set an excellent example as to how to avoid awkwardness: confidence! So long as you come across confidently, and speak at a decent volume, then there's no need to let embarrassment make an awkward atmosphere!

Am I overthinking things? I always get the feeling that George is looking down on us with utter disdain... But maybe I should keep it down, no matter how excited I am. It's late, after all, and I don't want to disturb the neighbors.
The arrival of the delivery guy certainly calms our friendly discussion. Stocked up with drinks and snacks, we press play once more on our viewing party...
I never made it to the end... I don't know when I dozed off, but the next thing I know I open my eyes and see the light outside...
...Got away with it.
Adventurers really are observant sorts. I stay silent for only a second, but he senses that something is off.

I lied. I was silent just now because what Joseph said actually made me a little uneasy. His attitude to exploring, and the sacrifices he's made to make progress... His kind of unrestrained manner is certainly impressive.

It's precisely because of his ability to decisively say goodbye to the past that I can't help but worry. I wonder if our memories together, as well as the other relationships he's formed in One Han City, might also one day become an impediment to his travels.
If this really is the case... How will Joseph deal with this bit of "the past"?
With drinks and snacks restocked, we press play on our viewing party once again. But I can't concentrate on the movie anymore, and that question is the only thing in my mind.
I can't think of an answer. Or maybe I should say... I dare not dwell on it.
And it's not like I can ask Joseph this directly...
I didn't see Joseph for a long time after our viewing party. So long, in fact, that people began to miss his hearty laughter at Mahjong tables.

As a busy adventurer, it wasn't strange that he wouldn't see anyone, being out and about from dawn to dusk. But every time I think back to our conversation that night, I can't help but feel a little uneasy.
I'm so anxious that I gradually start feeling as if he was never really here. This feeling grew only stronger after the discussion at the Mahjong table...
I have only myself to blame for not paying enough attention. I check, it's Riichi Ippatsu, and I just helped her get a high score with Pure Double Sequence...
{character:Joseph} ...
{character:George} ...
{character:player} ...
Are you leaving One Han City, Joseph?
I have only just spoken before I dealt into another Haneman, and bring the round to an early conclusion.
Months pass in the blink of an eye. The weather grows cold, with snowstorms practically every week this entire month.
This whole time, I still haven't seen Joseph. Maybe Kana was right, and he just slipped away from One Han City.
In pursuit of progress, maybe it's his old trick of nonchalantly bidding farewell to the "past"...
Today is Christmas Eve. This time last year, unbeknownst to us, Joseph had dressed up as Santa, and jumped from a helicopter to land at the shrine. It was a pretty great surprise.

Ichihime seems to have really been looking forward to it this year. So as her provider, it's fallen to me to play the part of Santa this year! I've prepared for this for many days, and spent so much money that it blew a hole in my wallet, but as long as people have fun, it'll be worth it.
That's what you thought too, right Joseph?

To be honest, I'm not as passionate as he was, and only wanted to do this due to some personal reasons. I think that by doing this, I can cheat myself... Give myself the illusion that he hasn't totally gone...
...Enough! No more thinking about Joseph. Gotta get my smile on! It's not right for Santa to be scowling!
Eh... Th-this laughter can't be...?!
I look back, only to see the Santa who just brushed past me remove his beard, and reveal a hearty, familiar smile.
I hesitate for a long while, before walking up to him, stretching out my hand, and gently pinching his face along the curve of his smiling lips.
I tell Joseph what happened that day at the Mahjong table, and he nods with a wry smile.
If anyone else had said that to me, I would have thought they were full of it. But it doesn't surprise me that such a thing could really happen to this guy.
Joseph stops walking and turns his head as he lights a cigarette. Walking in the direction he is now looking would, if I remember correctly, bring us to the One Han City port.

Language truly is power. With just a few words, it's possible to calm stormy emotions that have seethed for months... Actually, maybe it's better to say that it's just this man's strength. His obvious sincerity is enough to make anyone feel at ease.
The delicious aroma of cooking reaches us as we approach the shrine, accompanied by the intermittent sounds of laughter.
I should have said this to him a long time ago, but had just never found quite the right moment.
As the one who had seen him first, I feel I have the right to also be the first in telling him these obvious words...

{character:Joseph} No no no! You're my guest, and I must do my best to be an excellent host. You just sit right there and make yourself at home, my friend.

{character:player} Uh, seems like I misunderstood. I saw that there's only the most basic of daily necessities here, and figured you must have either just moved in or are in the process of moving out.

{character:player} On the way here I tried to imagine what your place was like. Now, I think it's... What's the best way to put this... A little too clean. Not quite what I thought an adventurer's place would be.

{character:Joseph} Hahaha! You really get me! Spot on, my friend. As long as someone I like is willing and able to look after and cherish an item, they can take whatever they want.

{character:Joseph} But I've had ample opportunity to enjoy the fruits of my labor. If I can share this joy with others, why not? Besides, by doing this I won't become possessed by these valuable possessions.
{character:player} That's really unfortunate.

{character:Joseph} Other people think I had an enviable collection of treasures that represented my past glory. But in reality, these treasures were slowly taking over my life. I could not bear to lose them, and could only let them multiply. At the worst, I had so many things that I could barely move around without stepping on something.
{character:player} That does sound like a hassle, having to always be mindful of where you walk. Or having to be careful in everything you do, really.
{character:Joseph} All that is only the physical aspect, too. The real trouble is the mental. You may find it hard to believe, but there was a brief period when I lost my passion for adventure.

{character:Joseph} Part of it was down to sheer physical exhaustion, but mostly it was due to waking up one day and finding the novelty of adventuring had worn off. I didn't know what to do, as everything seemed dull and drab.
{character:player} ...That is hard to imagine.
Joseph, tired of exploring...! Almost as believable as Jack and the Beanstalk.
{character:Joseph} Can't see it, right?! I had thought that nothing could ever make me tire of adventure, but the fact is, I spent almost a full year staying at home, doing nothing...
{character:Joseph} I felt completely lost during that time, with no idea what was wrong with me. The only thing I was sure of was that I was ill, and struggling with my mental health.
{character:Joseph} I saw a therapist several times, but their assessment of me came back as normal. Apart from losing my joie de vivre, my mood could be considered stable.
{character:Joseph} The therapist advised me to stop ruminating, and try to foster some other hobbies. While I could see the reason for this advice, I just didn't want to do it.

{character:Joseph} I got the stubborn idea into my head of wanting to identify what caused me to lose interest in adventure. I needed to know the reason, and bid a dignified farewell to the thing I used to love.
{character:Joseph} I was racking my brains to no avail, until one day an old friend I hadn't seen in a long time paid me a visit...
{character:Joseph} When I chose to give that object away, it was no longer just an ornament, but a symbol of friendship. It looked even more dazzling with that added layer of meaning.
{character:Joseph} And then suddenly—and I mean before I could blink—I had an epiphany.

{character:Joseph} I turned to look at my private collection of treasures, and found them oppressive. It's not like I suddenly detested them, but I had this incredible realization that my life had somehow been taken over by them.
{character:Joseph} I knew one thing for sure... I needed to say a proper goodbye, for all the adventures yet to come.

{character:Joseph} Value doesn't even come into it. Giving it away doesn't matter, so as long as it's to the right person. It's like that saying you have here, something about objects bound with people by fate.
{character:Joseph} This was definitely a difficult process. I asked myself on many occasions if I was being foolish.

{character:Joseph} But finally, as I surveyed the empty room, I felt that familiar fire come roaring over me, and knew it was all worthwhile... Fire, the fire that urged me to adventure, was blazing brightly once more...
{character:Joseph} By not allowing myself to have anything, I can avoid comparing the past with the present. Only then is it possible for me to move forward.
{character:player} ...You mean, you can't get excited by finding new treasures if you keep the old ones, because you'll have something similar in your collection already?

{character:Joseph} That's just it. Treasure-hunting was my motivation for adventuring. I don't want personal issues to cost my passion for finding treasure or respect for nature—to me, that's the height of arrogance. I had to find a way to keep myself hungry, and turn that hunger into action.

{character:Joseph} There's no way I can treat everything as truly unique, so can only use the somewhat clumsy "farewell" method. This helps me view the treasures at hand as unique as possible, so that every serendipitous encounter is full of excitement and surprise.

{character:Joseph} Okay! I've got some gifts for them. Can't wait to see how happy they are!

{character:Joseph} Our accident totally turned my friend off the idea of making an adventure show, so I can't do it even if I really wanted to!
{character:Joseph} I prefer the boss here. No matter how reckless I can be, I'm trusted to get the job done. Even if there are some places I can't go, I like the freedom I get working under him.
